turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I shall not be swayed by your taunts, Sandip. I have the law on my side, and I will not hesitate to enforce it if you continue to oppress my people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, you're so fond of talking about the law, but do you know the law of the zamindars? We don't need your permission to stay on our own land, do we?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not tolerate any further disregard for the law, Sandip. You may have the support of your followers, but I have the authority of the land on my side.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what's this, Nikhil? You think the law is some sacred cow you can trot out whenever it suits you? I've seen you use it to get rid of the very people who might have stood up to you if you'd treated them fairly.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in a debate with you, Sandip. My duty is to protect my people, and I will see to it that justice is served.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: I'm not afraid of your threats, Nikhil, and I'm certainly not going to be intimidated by your dramatics.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have come to give you one final warning, Sandip. Heed it, and perhaps we can avoid bloodshed.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, I'm shaking in my boots, Nikhil. Do tell me, what dreadful fate awaits me if I don't take your precious warning to heart?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be mocked, Sandip. My warning is not a jest, and I will not be ignored.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Come now, Nikhil, if I were to take your warnings seriously, I'd have to start wearing a helmet and a bulletproof vest just to walk out of my own house.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your flippant attitude, Sandip, only serves to underscore the gravity of the situation. I suggest you take a moment to consider the consequences of your actions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Do go on, Nikhil, tell me more about these dire consequences. I'm simply fascinated by your dire predictions.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not tolerate your insolence, Sandip. The situation is grave, and I will not be made a laughingstock by your flippant words.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, spare me the theatrics, Nikhil, I'm shaking in my boots. Do tell, what dire fate awaits me if I don't don a helmet and a vest?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in a battle of wits with you, Sandip. The situation is not a laughing matter, and I expect you to treat it with the gravity it deserves.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, you're such a card, always predicting doom and gloom, never a glimmer of hope. I'm surprised you don't offer to provide me with a helmet and a vest, along with your dire warnings.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I couldn't help but wonder, what evidence do you have for these potential attacks?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be questioned by anyone, least of all my wife. The matter at hand is one of duty and responsibility, not speculation.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, I think it would be helpful if you explained what specific actions you propose we take to prepare for these potential attacks.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Come now, Nikhil, spare me the elaborate scenarios. What's the worst they could do, burn down my poor estate? I'm shaking in my boots.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
